manual: Instructions for the Experiment Peeling and Observing the Internal Structure of a Soybean SeedI. Basic Experiment InformationExperiment Title: Peeling and Observing the Internal Structure of a Soybean SeedSubject: Engineering - Agricultural EngineeringExperiment Objective: To observe the internal structure of a soybean seed by manual dissection, verify that mature soybean seeds have no endosperm, and understand that two cotyledons fill the seed coat and wrap the hypocotyl and radicle.II. Experimental Materials and ToolsDry soybean seeds (1-2 grains), tweezers, clean tray or white paper, optional magnifying glass.III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Place a dry soybean seed on a clean tray or hold it steadily between fingers. Observe the intact seed coat.2. Peeling the Seed Coat: Use tweezers to gently pinch and peel off the seed coat from one side, removing it completely without damaging the inside.3. Separating the Seed: After removing the seed coat, gently separate the two halves of the seed with tweezers or fingers.4. Opening and Observation: Open the cotyledons to expose the internal embryo structure, including the hypocotyl and radicle.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. The dry soybean seed is covered by a thin seed coat.2. After peeling, the interior is completely filled by two large cotyledons.3. No endosperm is observed inside the seed.4. The hypocotyl and radicle are located between and wrapped by the two cotyledons.V. Summary of Experimental PrinciplesSoybean is a dicotyledonous plant. During seed development, nutrients are stored in the cotyledons rather than in the endosperm. As a result, mature soybean seeds lack endosperm, and the two cotyledons occupy nearly the entire interior of the seed coat while enclosing the embryo (hypocotyl and radicle).
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Soybean seed structure as a dicot seed without endosperm, composed mainly of two cotyledons enclosing the embryo. Minimum assumptions: the seed is dry and intact, basic hand tools are used, and the viewer has a clear view of the dissection. Expected phased storyline: (1) Initial state showing an intact dry soybean seed in hand; (2) Action phase where tweezers peel off the seed coat; (3) Separation phase where the seed splits into two cotyledons; (4) Final observation phase highlighting the absence of endosperm and the embryo wrapped by cotyledons. Visibility constraints: close-up perspective on the seed and hands, stable lighting, and clear focus on internal structures for verification.
